title: Ghouila–Houri theorem for directed Hamilton cycles
statement: Let $D$ be a loopless finite digraph on a vertex set of size $n > 2$, and suppose that every vertex $v$ satisfies $d^{-}(v) \ge n/2$ and $d^{+}(v) \ge n/2$, where $d^{-}(v)$ and $d^{+}(v)$ denote the indegree and outdegree of $v$. Then $D$ contains a directed cycle of length $n$; that is, a closed directed walk of positive length whose vertices, apart from the coinciding endpoints, are distinct, and which passes through every vertex of $D$.
hypotheses_covered: every vertex has indegree at least n/2 (n ≤ 2·d⁻(v))
every vertex has outdegree at least n/2 (n ≤ 2·d⁺(v))
